snippet.title: The Destroyer From Jail Longplay (Arcade) [4K]
snippet.description:
Game Info
---------------------------------------------------
Developer: Four J International
Publisher: Philko
Year of Release: 1991

Game Review & Impressions
---------------------------------------------------
From the darkest and remotest corners of the arcade obscura comes The Destroyer From Jail, a bizarre oddity from Philko and Four J International. The title and intro sequence gave me vibes of Marvel's The Punisher, although the only thing getting punished here is the poor player.

Although it doesn't appear to be listed as such, this feels almost like a bootleg of Tecmo's Shadow Warriors. The two-tier design of the levels is extremely similar, as is the destructible furniture scattered across the play-field. The artwork and levels appear to be original, although the audio effects most definitely aren't, with clips lifted from E-SWAT and RoboCop. It wasn't until after watching the footage back that I saw the parallels with NARC, which I reckon was probably one of the chief inspirations for this.

The game starts out with you gunning down balaclava-clad goons with UZIs and fedora-wearing gangsters, but it goes off the deep end soon after. You'll get into firefights with peg-legged pirates, cannon-wielding buccaneers, a multitude of ninjas, and even Frankenstein's monster! Perhaps the weirdest of all enemies is the tiny stilt-walker packing a flamethrower, and that's saying something.

I wish the game had been fun to play, but the truth of the matter is it just sucks. The rapidity of the timer and shonky hit detection help make this one of the most difficult -- and terrible -- games I've played in a long time. It's literally impossible not to lose lives here, so I guess it's fortunate that you can find bonus 1-Ups hidden in fuel drums and barrels. I was surprised to discover you can take cover behind certain obstacles, but it offers little advantage because the timer is so oppressive that you need to keep moving at all costs.

There's little else I can say about this, other than it's rather bonkers. It's an improvement on Philko's earlier games, but that's rally not saying very much. Try if you must, but you'll be sending this back to the depths of the obscura, if not in disgust, then certainly irritation.
